                 Dear Dr Waters
                 Re: Mrs Carol Potter                    DOB: 30/12/1947

                 I am writing to refer Mrs Potter, a 70-year-old retired assistant, whose symptoms and signs are suggestive of worsening of
                 osteoarthritis in the left knee. Your further management and possibility of a knee joint replacement would be highly appreciated.

                 Regarding the medical history of Mrs Potter, she has had an osteoarthritis in the hands and knees since 2008 and hypertension
                 since 2015. She is on Panadol Osteo and ramipril.

                 On 23/02/2018, Mrs Potter attended my clinic complaining of pain on the right knee especially after walking. The examination
                 revealed decrease the of movement of the left knee along with tenderness on pressure over the joint. An X-ray of the left knee and
                 blood tests was requested, naproxen 250mg was prescribed.

                 On todays visit, an X-ray show osteophytes and loss of the joint space which indicates sever osteoarthritis in the left knee, patella
                 was normal. Additionally, no fracture was noticed. The blood tests was unremarkable. Consequently, she was advised to undergo
                 physiotherapy and increasing the dose of analgesia.

                 In view of the above, it would be greatly appreciated if conduct further assessment of Mrs Potter’s condition and decide whether a
                 knee joint replacement is required.

                 Yours sincerely
                 Doctor
